  - Information criteria: `AIC()`, `BIC()`

- Use the **lab material** as an example

## Interpreting coefficients is harder

A logistic regression coefficient can be expressed on three scales:

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div class="flow-row">
    <div class="step"><b>Log-odds</b><small>&beta;: additive change<br>in the logit</small></div>
    <div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
    <div class="step final"><b>Odds ratio</b><small>e<sup>&beta;</sup>: odds are<br>multiplied by this</small></div>
    <div class="arrow">&rarr;</div>
    <div class="step"><b>Probability</b><small>&pi; = odds / (1 + odds)<br>not a constant effect</small></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

- e<sup>β</sup> \> 1: higher odds of the outcome; e<sup>β</sup> \< 1: lower odds
- Odds ratio below 1? Its reciprocal (1 / e<sup>β</sup>) is often easier to explain

## Example: passing an exam

logit(passing) = −3.414 + 0.683 × study hours

- **Intercept:** a student who does not study has log-odds of passing of −3.41, so odds of e<sup>−3.414</sup> = **0.03**
- **Slope:** each extra hour of study increases the log-odds by 0.683, so the **odds** of passing are multiplied by e<sup>0.683</sup> = **1.98**

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" style="font-size: 1.25em;"}
Odds are not probabilities: 1.98 times the **odds** of passing is not 1.98 times the **probability** of passing!
:::

## Example: surviving the Titanic

`glm(survived ~ age + sex + class, family = "binomial")`

::: gradetable
| Term | β | Odds ratio | Interpretation (controlling for the other predictors) |
|----------|-------:|---------:|--------------------------------------------|
| age | −0.034 | 0.97 | Each extra year: odds of survival × 0.97 |
| sexmale | −2.589 | 0.08 | Men: 0.08 times the odds of survival of women, or 13.3 times the odds of **death** |
| class3rd | −2.455 | 0.09 | 3rd vs 1st class: 0.09 times the odds of survival, or 11.7 times the odds of death |
:::

## Making a presentation in Quarto

- Use `format: revealjs` in the YAML header
- Each `##` heading starts a new slide
- Keep slides **concise**: little text, meaningful visuals, no long code blocks
- Add `embed-resources: true`, so your slides are one self-contained .html file

More tips: open-stat-prog module [Creating presentations with Quarto](https://www.openstatprog.com/reproducible-reporting/tutorials/quarto_markdown/presentations.html)
